data.name: Settings_Agent_Elevation_Body
data.value: Elevation is not required by any capture tier. It optionally unlocks CPU temperature (through PawnIO) and attaching to games that run elevated themselves. Everything else — hooking, measuring, recording — works without it.

data.value: Applied. The capture agent reads it at the next session start.

data.name: Settings_Background_Body
data.value: The capture agent watches for tracked games; a game it did not launch is recorded, and measured only if hooking is on for it and it is not a Vulkan title.

data.name: Settings_Interval_Body
data.value: How often hardware telemetry is sampled during a session (500–2000).

data.name: Settings_KillSwitch_Body

data.name: Settings_LogDebug_Body

data.name: Settings_OnlineMetadata_Body

data.name: Settings_Retention_Body

data.name: Settings_SafetyDocs

data.name: Settings_VkLayer_Note
data.value: Registration puts the layer into every Vulkan process of this user, where it stays inert unless FrameLedger launched that process. Launching from FrameLedger needs no registration. The capture agent registers the layer on its own while a hook-enabled game references the Vulkan loader and removes it when the last one is disabled; the buttons repair that state and are allowed only under the same rule.

data.name: FirstRun_Agent_Body
data.value: FrameLedger starts a small capture agent beside itself, as a standard user — not elevated. Elevation is optional and is not required by any capture tier: it only unlocks CPU temperature (through PawnIO) and attaching to games that run elevated themselves. Below is what the agent reports about this machine.

data.name: FirstRun_Explainer_Intro
data.value: FrameLedger measures a game by loading a library into its process — hooking. Hooking is off for every game until you enable it for that game, one at a time, after a dialog that repeats what is written here. The Disclaimer you accepted states the risk; this screen states what each choice records.

data.name: FirstRun_Explainer_Off
data.value: Nothing changes until you add a game and enable hooking for it. Every game you add starts with hooking off.

data.name: FirstRun_Import_Body
data.value: FrameLedger can read what Steam, GOG Galaxy, Epic and itch.io have installed and add them from a checklist — File ▸ Import library… on the Games page, once you are in. Every imported game starts with hooking off, exactly like one you add by hand.

data.name: FirstRun_Legal_Body
data.value: Four documents describe what this software does, what it does not do, and what it may cost you. Please read them; Accept covers all four. Declining closes FrameLedger.

data.name: Maintenance_Intro
data.value: Your sessions live in one SQLite file, the ledger. Checking and backing up only read it. Compacting rewrites the file with the same contents and waits until no session runs. Sweeping removes raw series by your retention setting; the Agent does it, because those rows are the Agent's.

data.name: Maintenance_Backup_Body

data.name: Maintenance_Backup_IsLedger

data.name: Maintenance_Sweep_Body
data.value: Removes the per-frame and sensor series of all but the newest sessions per game, as the retention setting says. Averages, percentiles and charts' summary rows stay.

data.name: FirstRun_Legal_Summary
data.value: In short — please read before you accept: • This is a beta (pre-release). It certainly still has bugs, and the developer is not responsible for problems that result. • Your PC must meet at least the minimum requirements the game's developer or publisher states. Read them first. Problems on a PC below them are your responsibility, not FrameLedger's. • Hooking loads a component into a game, one game at a time, only after you agree. Anti-cheat systems can ban an account for that. FrameLedger refuses where it detects anti-cheat and turns hooking off for that game; there is no way to override that refusal. • Nothing is sent anywhere. Your recordings stay on this PC, and backing them up is up to you. The documents below are the full terms; this summary does not replace them.
